# <span id="aanchor177"></span> <span id="aanchor178"></span> Configure File Imports

The File Import service is a Windows service that must be installed on the application server where FLOWCAL is installed. Depending on operation size (number of meters, locations, hardware specifications), customers may have multiple application servers, each server having the capacity to run one or more import services.

Running multiple import services allows FLOWCAL to distribute the work of importing data across multiple services instead of a single service.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

If a customer has 60,000 meters, instead of one service processing 60,000 meters on one server, they could run eight services across two servers (four on each server). Running multiple services would divide the workload by eight, so each service is handling no more than 7,500 meters at any time.

</div>

Contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="InlineLink">Customer Support</a> for recommendations on how many file import services to run for the FLOWCAL installation.

<span id="Common_Import_File_Types"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Import File Types">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Common Import File Types</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Import File Types">

Most files imported into FLOWCAL are in Quorum’s proprietary CFX file format. The service can also be used to import meter and quality source text files for gas or liquid meters, as well as other meter file types.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 676;height: 373;" />

Windows does not allow the \\ / : \* ? " \< \> \| characters in import file names.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="CFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />CFX Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="CFX">

A CFX (Common File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to bring meter flow data and configuration information into FLOWCAL. It is used to import data from a variety of meter manufacturers.

SCADA systems generate CFX files using one of the following formats:

- **Datetime Stamped CFX File Names within a Folder Structure** - A folder structure must be created with each meter number as a folder name. CFX files are created within each folder with the datetime stamp as the file name, where file name format is “YYMMDDSQ.CFX” or “YYYYMMDDSQ.CFX” where SQ is a sequence number. The sequence number is only used when multiple files are generated for the same day.

Note that the year, month, and day in the file name does not have to match the year month and day of data in the CFX file. If a file contains data for an entire month, the "DD" value will be "00".

> FLOWCAL will only process 35 days of data, regardless of how many files have been read.

- **CFX File Names by Meter Number** - A CFX file with the meter number as the file name does not need meter subfolders. The CFX files can be imported from a main directory and there will be an individual file for each meter. Each time a CFX file is created, it must have the same file name as the previous file created for that meter.

> The system creating the CFX files will typically overwrite an existing file when new data comes in. As a result, a process for saving files for audit purposes may be necessary. The FLOWCAL file import service will rename or relocate processed files.

- **Combination** - You may see a combination of both methods if you have multiple SCADA systems; some systems may create the folder structure and others may generate files using the meter number (see figure above). This is an acceptable practice as long as files for a given meter are created using the same method every time.

See also: [Import Meter Data](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Data.md)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="TFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />TFX Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="TFX">

A TFX (Ticket File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to import volume and accounting information from run tickets and gauge tickets (such as pipelines, LACTs, trucks, railcars, marine vessels, or tank tickets) into FLOWCAL. Each ticket record in a TFX file is mapped to a FLOWCAL ticket by the ticket ID contained in the record.

A folder named “TFXFiles” must be created in the main import directory defined in the FLOWCAL Service Configuration screen. This folder is where the File Import service will import the TFX files from.

<div class="example">

**Example:** "C:\\FCImport\TFXFiles"

</div>

See also: [Import Ticket Data](../Imports/Import%20Ticket%20Data.md)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="PFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />PFX Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="PFX">

A PFX (Prove Report File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to import liquid product prover data. The format encompasses prove results, prove run, and pass data, and prover and product identification. PFX files are mapped to a meter by the meter number. The directory for the File Import service to import PFX files from is set on the Liquids tab of the FLOWCAL Service Configuration screen.

See also: [Import Prove Data](../Imports/Import%20Prove%20Data.md)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Gast Text Files">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Gas Meter Text Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="background-color: #ffffff; display: none;" mc-target-name="Gast Text Files">

Text files can be used to import gas meter data in the format specified by FLOWCAL (contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="InlineLink">Customer Support</a> for the file format). These files can be used to import data for one or more meters.

A folder named "MeterTextFiles" must be created in the main import directory. This folder is where the File Import service will import the text files from.

<div class="example">

**Example:** "C:\\FCImport\MeterTextFiles"

</div>

When importing gas meter data text files by meter import ID, a folder named “MeterTextFilesByImportID” must be created in the main import directory.

<div class="example">

**Example:** "C:\\FCImport\MeterTextFilesByImportID"

</div>

See also: [Import Meter Text File (Gas)](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Text%20File%20-%20Gas.md)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Liquid Ticket">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Folder Security">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Folder Security</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Folder Security">

Folder security must be configured to allow the File Import service read/write access to the import directory.

<div class="procedure">

To set the folder security on the main import directory:

1.  Go to the folder where the import files will be imported from (example: "C:\\FCImport").
2.  Right-click the folder and select **Properties**.
3.  Click the **Security** tab and click **Edit**.
4.  Select the Windows account used for the service logon (configured on the service in Windows Services console). The account permissions should include all options excluding Special Permissions and Full Control. If the folder is shared, it must also have read and execute permissions.
5.  Click **Apply** and close the window.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Service Configuration">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />FLOWCAL Service Configuration</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Service Configuration">

The Service Configuration screen is used to configure the FLOWCAL services installed on the application servers. Before starting the File Import service, a FLOWCAL service account must be configured, which the service will use to log onto the database.

Most companies create a user name called "FCSRV" to easily identify the credentials.

The administrator defines the network location where FLOWCAL imports files from. Typically, there is a directory specified on the same server where FLOWCAL is installed (Example: "D:\\FCImport"); however, a directory on another server can also be specified.

Do not start the File Import service until all setup and configuration is complete.

<div class="procedure">

To configure a service account:

1.  Right-click the **FLOWCAL.exe** file as select **Run as Administrator**.
2.  Log in to FLOWCAL and open the Service Configuration screen from the Settings Manager (**Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Service Configuration**).
3.  Click **Edit** and enter your login credentials.
4.  Click the **File Imports** tab at the bottom of the screen. Use the **Folder to Check** field to specify the folder to import from.
5.  Click **Save**.

If the File Import service is currently running, you must restart it for the new settings to take place.

When determining the Total FLOWCAL Installations value, consider the number of File Import services installed against the highest number of other services, and enter the highest number of the two. For example: If you are running four File Import services, three Meter Rollup services and one of each of the other services, enter "4". Count each service on all machines collectively, regardless of whether they are on separate servers. This helps maintain efficiency across services that require more resources.  

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Configure Meters for CFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Configuring Meter Imports for CFX</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Configure Meters for CFX">

If you are importing meter data using CFX files, each meter must be configured. This can be done manually in the Meter Editor or in bulk using the Bulk Changes screen or the FcLoader utility.

<div class="procedure">

To configure meter imports from the Meter Editor:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**.

2.  Select a meter.

3.  Click the **Imports** tab, and click the **Edit** button.

4.  Choose a driver under the **File Options** section.

    Most users will import CFX files, so most will select the STNDCFX driver.

5.  Browse to the import directory to select an import path (folder), or copy and paste the import path.

6.  If you are receiving CFX files using datetime stamped file names, select an import file sub-folder. If you are selecting CFX files named by meter name, select a file name.

    A file path is not required on the Meter Editor for FLOWCAL’s standard text file imports; however, when using an import ID, the import ID must be defined on each meter.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Configuring Meters for txt">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Configuring Meter Imports For Text Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Configuring Meters for txt">

A file path is not required at the meter level for FLOWCAL’s standard text file imports; however, when using an import ID, this must be defined on the Imports tab of the Meter Editor for each meter.

See <a href="#Common_Import_File_Types" class="InlineLink"></a><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Import File Types">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Common Import File Types</a>.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Configure Sources for txt">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Configuring Source Quality Imports for Text Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Configure Sources for txt">

A file path is not required at the source quality level for FLOWCAL’s standard text file imports; however, when using an import ID, this must be defined on the Main tab of the Quality Source Editor.

See <a href="#Common_Import_File_Types" class="InlineLink"></a><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Import File Types">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Common Import File Types</a>.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Starting File Import Service">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Running the File Import Service</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Starting File Import Service">

Once the File Import service is installed and configured, a Windows administrator can start the service.

<div class="procedure">

To run the service:

1.  Click the Windows **Start** button. Type “Services” in the find field, and press **Enter**. This launches the Windows Services console.
2.  Scroll down the services list to find the File Import service (FcSrvFileImport).
3.  Right-click the service name and select **Start**.

You can view the status of the service from the [Service Monitor](../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Monitor.md).

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Renaming Files">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Renaming Processed Files</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Renaming Files">

The File Import service scans each subfolder and file in the specified import folder (Ex. C:\\FCImport), and then searches FLOWCAL for a matching path and file name (see Meter Editor \> Imports tab: "Import Path (Folder)" and "Subfolder or Filename") to establish a mapping. If a file is not mapped to a meter within FLOWCAL, it will not be processed.

The File Import service utilizes control files to minimize "hanging" instances during which the import of a corrupt file is repeatedly attempted. Once a file or folder is locked for processing, a local control file is created (upon first import attempt) or updated. The control file tracks the attempts made to import the file by recording an informational entry on each attempt. The entry consists of the date and time of the attempt and the service executable that made the attempt. If the configurable number of retries is reached (Settings Manager \> Service Configuration \> File Imports \> Number of retries) and the file has not imported, then no further attempts are made, the file or folder is marked as failed, and the failure is reported via a system message.

#### File Extensions

Import file extensions will be updated to include the state of the file and the processing date and time.
